overview: This table gathers each character's sound setup, including audio that loads early, footstep sounds, battle voices, and menu or result lines.
description: Per-character/variation sound bundle: cue sheets to preload, the footstep family, candidate CharacterVoiceGroupSet rows for battle voices, and system/menu VoiceGroup IDs.

Id.simple: The name that identifies this sound setup. The game follows it from a character version or shikigami, and also when a menu or result voice is requested.
Id.technical: FName FindRow key; the single export has 56 unique keys and its IDs all equal their row keys. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows selects CharacterVariation.Id_CharacterVariation[InVariationIndex] without an index check, then uses Overrides.SoundIdOverride when non-None, otherwise Variation.Id_CharacterSound; mission-character setup can copy MissionCharacter.Id_CharacterSound into that override. The result is cached at AGameCharacter+0x3D0 and a miss fails the whole character setup. AGameShikigami resolves Shikigami.Id_CharacterSound through the shared finder (with None rejected) and caches a possibly null row at +0x350. Sequencer NPCs use the skinned-model name as the key, while UGameSoundVoicePlayer first resolves a supplied CharacterVariation ID and then uses that variation's Id_CharacterSound. Every finder walks DTM.CharacterSoundDataTables (+0x510) and returns the first typed row.

CueSheetName.simple: Changes which sound collections load before a match or character preview so their audio is ready. Blank entries are ignored, and some characters also load a second collection.
CueSheetName.technical: TArray<FName>; it is a preload list, not an index into the other voice arrays. BattleAssets_CueSheets_12BC230 finds the row from CharacterVariation.Id_CharacterSound and appends every entry verbatim; battle preload, IntervalPvE and LevelSequencer feed such lists to LoadCueSheets. The situation-overview widget filters None before LoadCueSheets, UnloadCueSheets and AreCueSheetsLoaded; the sound manager also ignores None and de-duplicates names, so an unfiltered placeholder does not create a load. All 56 exported rows have two entries: 46 are [named sheet, None], 8 pair a second (often another character's) sheet, and 2 are [None, None]. These collectors use the base variation's Id_CharacterSound and do not apply the battle SoundIdOverride.

FootstepType.simple: Changes whether footsteps sound like men's shoes, women's shoes, bare feet, zori, gorilla steps, or Totality. Choosing no type plays no footstep sound.
FootstepType.technical: EGameFootstepType (uint8): None=0, ShoesMan=1, ShoesWoman=2, BareFoot=3, Zori=4, Gorilla=5, Totality=6, Invalid=255; the row constructor defaults it to None. AGameCharacter::GetFootstepType returns the cached row value with no null guard; AGameShikigami::GetFootstepType returns 0 if its cached row is null; sequencer NPCs read the row directly by model-name key and return 0 when no row is found. The footstep notify needs a MapGround row, converts the value with GameAnimNotify_TypeIndex (value - 1), and indexes GroundRow.Id_SoundEffect_Footstep only when 0 <= Index < Num: values 1-6 select indices 0-5, None gives -1 and Invalid gives 254, both selecting nothing. All 56 exported rows populate this field: 19 ShoesMan, 14 BareFoot, 7 ShoesWoman, 6 Zori, 4 Gorilla, 4 Totality and 2 None; Invalid is unused. Each of the eight MapGround rows supplies six valid SoundEffect IDs.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet.simple: Chooses which sets of spoken lines the fighter uses for attacks, other actions, and low health.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet.technical: TArray<FName>; all 56 exported rows have four entries (three rows are all None), commonly default/TypeA/TypeB/PINCH. ActionController slot 90 normally returns this array by value from the cached SoundRow. AGameCharacter::FindCharacterVoiceGroupSetRow(Mode) uses Mode 0 and 3 directly as indices, but Mode 1 substitutes NormalAttackVoiceIndex and Mode 2 CursedEnergyAttackVoiceIndex; those setup values come from UserCustomizeVoiceInfo and default to 0. Out-of-range or None entries resolve to no row, and the first matching CharacterVoiceGroupSetDataTables row wins. In PlayVoice, kinds 1/3/4 choose Mode 1, kind 2 takes the attack action's mode, kinds 5/10 choose Mode 2, others use Mode 0; when the applicable HP check passes (max HP <= 0 or HP/max <= 0.3) Mode becomes 3. Kind 1 disables that check, kind 4 checks only Index 2, and kind 5 checks only Indexes 2, 5 and 6. CP_051 is an alias: while its passive is active, its controller overrides slot 90 with hardcoded CP_051_2 / CP_051_TYPEA_2 / CP_051_TYPEB_2 / CP_051_PINCH_2 instead of this field.

Id_VoiceGroup.simple: Chooses the spoken lines for moments like picking a character, seeing results, or asking for a rematch. A blank leaves that moment silent.
Id_VoiceGroup.technical: TArray<FName>; every exported row has exactly 20 entries, matching EGameCharacterSoundVoiceGroupType values 1-20 positionally. UGameSoundVoicePlayer::PlayCharacterVoice resolves the supplied CharacterVariation ID, finds this row through that variation's Id_CharacterSound, computes GroupKind - 1 with GameAnimNotify_TypeIndex, and reads Sound->Id_VoiceGroup[GroupIndex] without a bounds check: GroupKind 0 gives -1 and values above 20 read past the end. A None ID stops the VoiceGroup lookup (bCheckNone=true). A VoiceGroup's Id_Voice entries are weighted 1.0 when non-None and 0.0 when None; the weighted lottery therefore picks uniformly among its non-None voices and returns nothing if all are None. All exported VoiceGroups referenced here have one non-None voice plus four None entries, and 21 sound rows have all 20 IDs set to None. The enum order is select/reselect, ready, two lobby lines, S/A/B-or-lower rank, four win-streak tiers, result item, two rank changes and five rematch outcomes. Traced requests use 1, 3, 4, 5, 6-15 and 16-20 via character select/menu, lobby, result widgets and the rematch-outcome mapping.

notes: Loaded as a 'DataTable' primary asset named CharacterSoundDataTable into DTM.CharacterSoundDataTables (+0x510). Character setup resolves the row from the selected variation plus a possible SoundIdOverride and caches it at AGameCharacter+0x3D0; a failed resolution fails that setup. Shikigami resolution is non-fatal and may leave a null cached row.

This row is a hub, not a leaf: Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet joins to CharacterVoiceGroupSetDataTable, Id_VoiceGroup joins to VoiceGroupDataTable and then VoiceDataTable, FootstepType joins indirectly through MapGround.Id_SoundEffect_Footstep to SoundEffectDataTable, and CueSheetName names loadable CRI sheets.

The base-variation cue-sheet preload path does not use SoundIdOverride, while live character setup and action voices do. CP_051 can additionally replace the voice-set ID array while its passive is active.

The export contains one CharacterSoundDataTable with 56 rows and no duplicate keys; 53 of its IDs are referenced by CharacterVariation rows (three rows are not directly referenced there). All non-None joins to CharacterVariation, CharacterVoiceGroupSet and VoiceGroup resolve in the supplied exports. These are available-content observations, not a completeness claim for retail or Blueprint references.
Runtime descriptions are based on reconstructed C++ with inline retail RVAs. The project guide attributes gameplay logic to C++. Blueprint asset wiring remains unverified.

usages.detail: Resolves the loaded CharacterSoundDataTable into DTM.CharacterSoundDataTables.
Resolves and caches the character's sound row during setup; a miss fails setup.
Copies MissionCharacter.Id_CharacterSound into the character setup's SoundIdOverride.
Shared typed first-match finder over CharacterSound tables.
Collects every CueSheetName entry for battle preloading.
Finds ally sound rows and filters None cue sheets for load, unload and readiness checks.
Exposes FootstepType through the actor interface.
Converts the footstep type to a bounds-checked index into MapGround footstep sounds.
Returns Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet from the cached sound row.
Selects and resolves a CharacterVoiceGroupSet row by mode and index.
Overrides slot 90 with hardcoded passive-specific voice-set IDs.
Resolves Id_VoiceGroup and queues a voice from the selected VoiceGroup.
Looks up footstep type by sequencer NPC model name.
